message.partialBody: Warp used all of its research steps before it finished checking. This is what it found so far, and it says what it could not confirm. A narrower question usually completes.

not_configured.cause: No provider and model are set, or Warp is switched off in settings.
suggestions: Open Warp settings and choose a provider and model.
Make sure Enable Warp is switched on.

max_iterations.summary: Warp could not settle on an answer.
max_iterations.cause: Warp ran its full budget of research steps without reaching a conclusion. That usually means the question was broad enough that each query raised another, so it kept looking instead of answering.
suggestions: Ask for one thing at a time: a single metric, one time range, one scope.
Name the window explicitly, for example 'in the last 24 hours'.
Name whose traffic you mean - a team, a customer, or all of them.
Raise Max Iterations in Warp settings if the question genuinely needs more steps.

timeout.cause: The whole request passed its time budget before Warp finished. Long time ranges and wide scopes make every query slower, and Warp runs several.
suggestions: Narrow to one team, customer or virtual key.
Raise Request Timeout in Warp settings if your model is simply slow.

upstream_error.summary: Warp's model could not be reached.
upstream_error.cause: The provider rejected the request or was unreachable. This is about Warp's own model, not the traffic you asked about.
suggestions: Check the provider, model and key in Warp settings.
Confirm the Base URL is right - it defaults to this Bifrost.
Try the same model from the playground to see whether it answers at all.

tool_error.cause: One of Warp's data queries returned an error, and it could not recover within its remaining steps.
suggestions: Check that the model, key or team you named actually exists.

cancelled.cause: The request was cancelled before it finished.

unknown.cause: Warp returned an error without a recognised code.
suggestions: If it keeps happening, report it with the details below.
